_meta.note: Every visible string of the front door, the tool page /t/<id>/, the result page /r/<id>/, the pricing and the status pages. Each message holds its text (or, for a count, one form per plural category of the language, chosen by {n}), a description of where it appears and what it does, for the translator, and max_length, the longest a translation may be: IBM's allowance for the English length (U7 R5, R31). {name} is filled in.

err.empty.text: Your file is empty, so I have nothing to check yet. Choose a file or paste a table, then press Check my data.
err.empty.description: An error shown in place of a result; it speaks as Knos, in the first person, and keeps the person's file: no file.

err.limit.text: I need the limit as a number, such as 1.4, before I can check your file. Please type it, then press Check my data.
err.limit.description: An error shown in place of a result; it speaks as Knos, in the first person, and keeps the person's file: no limit typed.

err.stopped.text: I stopped the check. Your file is still in the box, so you can change it or try again.
err.stopped.description: An error shown in place of a result; it speaks as Knos, in the first person, and keeps the person's file: the person stopped the run.

err.reach.description: An error shown in place of a result; it speaks as Knos, in the first person, and keeps the person's file: the server did not answer.

err.none.text: I could not get a result from Knos's server just now. Your file is still in the box, so press Try again in a moment.
err.none.description: An error shown in place of a result; it speaks as Knos, in the first person, and keeps the person's file: the server answered with no result.

err.too_big.one: Your file is too big. The limit is {n} row. I kept your file in the box; try a shorter one.
err.too_big.other: Your file is too big. The limit is {n} rows. I kept your file in the box; try a shorter one.
err.too_big.description: An error shown in place of a result; it speaks as Knos, in the first person, and keeps the person's file: the file has too many rows. Keep {n} as written; it is filled in. One form per plural category of the language, chosen by {n}.

err.too_long.one: This took too long and was stopped. Try a smaller file. I stopped it after {n} second and kept your file in the box.
err.too_long.other: This took too long and was stopped. Try a smaller file. I stopped it after {n} seconds and kept your file in the box.
err.too_long.description: An error shown in place of a result; it speaks as Knos, in the first person, and keeps the person's file: the run took too long. Keep {n} as written; it is filled in. One form per plural category of the language, chosen by {n}.

err.not_ready.text: I cannot check files yet, because the program for this tool has not passed the test that decides it works. Please try again later.
err.not_ready.description: An error shown in place of a result; it speaks as Knos, in the first person, and keeps the person's file: the tool's program has not passed its test yet.

err.bad.text: I could not read your file with these settings. Check the column and the limit; your file is still in the box.
err.bad.description: An error shown in place of a result; it speaks as Knos, in the first person, and keeps the person's file: the file cannot be read with these settings.

chart.row.description: The chart of the result: the mark on the first failing row. Keep {r} as written; it is filled in.

rs.fail_above.text: Failed at row {r}: {value} is not above {limit}.
rs.fail_above.description: Part of the result sentence, built from the program's English sentence: a value was not above the limit. Keep {limit}, {r}, {value} as written; they are filled in.

rs.fail_below.text: Failed at row {r}: {value} is not below {limit}.
rs.fail_below.description: Part of the result sentence, built from the program's English sentence: a value was not below the limit. Keep {limit}, {r}, {value} as written; they are filled in.

rs.cannot.text: I cannot check: no row has a number.
rs.cannot.description: The whole result when no row held a number, so nothing was checked (never a pass); said in the first person, UX/U6.md Rule 7.

rs.pass_above.description: Part of the result sentence, built from the program's English sentence: every row was above the limit. Keep {limit}, {n} as written; they are filled in. One form per plural category of the language, chosen by {n}.

rs.pass_below.description: Part of the result sentence, built from the program's English sentence: every row was below the limit. Keep {limit}, {n} as written; they are filled in. One form per plural category of the language, chosen by {n}.

rs.passed.description: Part of the result sentence, after a failing row: how many rows passed. Keep {n} as written; it is filled in. One form per plural category of the language, chosen by {n}.

rs.unchecked_one.text: Row {r} has no number, so I did not check it.
rs.unchecked_one.description: Part of the result sentence: the one row whose cell is missing or not a number, so it was not checked; said in the first person, UX/U6.md Rule 7. Keep {r} as written; it is filled in.

rs.unchecked.text: Rows {rows} have no number, so I did not check them.
rs.unchecked.description: Part of the result sentence: two or more rows whose cells are missing or not numbers, so they were not checked; said in the first person. {rows} is the list of row numbers built with rs.list_sep and rs.list_and or rs.list_more. Keep {rows} as written.

rs.list_sep.description: The separator between row numbers in a list of rows that were not checked (for example the comma in 2, 5 and 7), as the language writes a list.

rs.list_and.description: The end of a list of row numbers (2, 5 and 7): {list} is the rows before the last, joined by rs.list_sep; {r} is the last row. Keep {list}, {r} as written.

rs.list_more.description: A list of the first five row numbers that were not checked, then how many more were not checked (2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 4 more). Keep {list}, {n} as written; they are filled in.

ask.holds.description: The question box below the tool on the front door, which answers from the proved claims: the claim holds.

ask.fails.description: The question box below the tool on the front door, which answers from the proved claims: the claim fails.

ask.not_yet.description: The question box below the tool on the front door, which answers from the proved claims: the claim is not proved yet.

ask.proved.text: Checked by a test set before any work started.
ask.proved.description: The question box below the tool on the front door, which answers from the proved claims: how the claim was proved.

ask.locked.text: Its test is locked before any work starts.
ask.locked.description: The question box below the tool on the front door, which answers from the proved claims: when the claim's test was locked.

ask.behind.text: {amount} in test money from people outside Knos this week
ask.behind.description: The question box below the tool on the front door, which answers from the proved claims: test money people outside Knos put behind the claim. Keep {amount} as written; it is filled in.

ask.prove.description: The question box below the tool on the front door, which answers from the proved claims: the link to prove the claim yourself.

ask.claim.description: The question box below the tool on the front door, which answers from the proved claims: the label of the claim.

ask.none.description: The question box below the tool on the front door, which answers from the proved claims: no proved claim matches.

ask.none_line.one: Knos has checked {n} claim; none is about "{q}". Ask about one of them, or enter a paper's link.
ask.none_line.other: Knos has checked {n} claims; none is about "{q}". Ask about one of them, or enter a paper's link.
ask.none_line.description: The question box below the tool on the front door, which answers from the proved claims: no proved claim matches, with what to do. Keep {n}, {q} as written; they are filled in. One form per plural category of the language, chosen by {n}.

ask.notwhat.description: The question box below the tool on the front door, which answers from the proved claims: the button to say the answer is not what was needed.

ask.why.description: The question box below the tool on the front door, which answers from the proved claims: the hint of the field for a one-word reason.

ask.why_label.description: The question box below the tool on the front door, which answers from the proved claims: the name of that field.

ask.thanks.description: The question box below the tool on the front door, which answers from the proved claims: after the reason is sent.

ask.noted.description: The question box below the tool on the front door, which answers from the proved claims: after the button is pressed.

ask.reading_paper.description: The question box below the tool on the front door, which answers from the proved claims: while a paper is read. Keep {s} as written; it is filled in.

ask.not_read.description: The question box below the tool on the front door, which answers from the proved claims: the paper was not read.

ask.no_answer.text: Knos's server did not answer, so the paper was not read. It may be waking up.
ask.no_answer.description: The question box below the tool on the front door, which answers from the proved claims: the server did not answer.

ask.cannot.text: Knos cannot check this paper yet
ask.cannot.description: The question box below the tool on the front door, which answers from the proved claims: the paper cannot be proved yet.

ask.person.text: Today a person checks it: {checker}. Price: {price_text}. Time: {time}.
ask.person.description: The question box below the tool on the front door, which answers from the proved claims: who checks the paper today, the price and the time. Keep {checker}, {price_text}, {time} as written; they are filled in.

ask.someone.description: The question box below the tool on the front door, which answers from the proved claims: the checker when no name is known.

ask.unpublished.description: The question box below the tool on the front door, which answers from the proved claims: a price or time that is not published.

ask.source.description: The question box below the tool on the front door, which answers from the proved claims: the link to the paper.

price.title.description: The pricing page: the browser tab's title.

price.h.description: The pricing page: the page's heading.

price.sample_free.text: Runs on the sample are free.
price.sample_free.description: The pricing page: a line saying sample runs cost nothing.

price.own.description: The pricing page: a row of the price table: the person's own file.

price.free_day.one: {n} free a day, in each browser
price.free_day.other: {n} free a day, in each browser
price.free_day.description: The pricing page: the free runs a day. Keep {n} as written; it is filled in. One form per plural category of the language, chosen by {n}.

price.after.description: The pricing page: the row after the free runs.

price.f1.text: No study gave these prices. They are starting values to be tested, and each one is in the pricing file with that mark.
price.f1.description: The pricing page: where the prices come from. Keep {url} as written; it is filled in. Keep the link markup.

price.f2.text: When your free runs are used up, the tool shows one screen with the price. Pressing Pay with test money records a test payment on Knos's own server. No card and no account are needed.
price.f2.description: The pricing page: how the pay screen works.

price.f3.text: The fees for checking a paper's claim are on a page of their own.
price.f3.description: The pricing page: where the fees for checking a claim are. Keep {url} as written; it is filled in. Keep the link markup.

nf.title.description: The page shown for an address that does not exist: the browser tab's title.

nf.h.description: The page shown for an address that does not exist: the page's heading.

nf.p.text: I have nothing at this address. A result may have been cleared when the Knos server was updated.
nf.p.description: The page shown for an address that does not exist: why the page is missing.

nf.link.text: Open the Knos tool and check a file
nf.link.description: The page shown for an address that does not exist: the link back to the tool.

res.cut.description: The result area, after a run: when a long file is shown cut short. Keep {n}, {shown} as written; they are filled in. One form per plural category of the language, chosen by {n}.

v.pass.description: The verdict word beside the result's icon: every row passed.

v.fail.description: The verdict word beside the result's icon: a row failed.

v.unknown.description: The verdict word beside the result's icon: Knos cannot tell.

ev.pass.description: The evidence line under the verdict: the rows compared. Keep {column}, {limit}, {n} as written; they are filled in. One form per plural category of the language, chosen by {n}.

ev.fail.description: The evidence line under the verdict: the row that failed. Keep {column}, {limit}, {r}, {value} as written; they are filled in.

why.unknown.description: The reason line under the result I cannot check: two or more rows whose cell in the column is missing or not a number, named by row. {rows} is the list of row numbers built with rs.list_sep and rs.list_and or rs.list_more (at most five numbers, then how many more). Keep {rows}, {column} as written; they are filled in.

next.pass.text: Every row passed: check your own file with Use my data.
next.pass.description: The next step line under a verdict: after a pass.

next.fail.text: Open your file at row {r}, the first row that failed.
next.fail.description: The next step line under a verdict: after a fail. Keep {r} as written; it is filled in.

next.unknown.text: Pick a column where each row holds a number, then press Check my data.
next.unknown.description: The next step line under a verdict: after a result Knos cannot tell.

work.rows.description: The waiting line while the server checks a file: the rows the run will check, shown at once. Keep {n} as written; it is filled in. One form per plural category of the language, chosen by {n}.

err.column.text: I cannot find a column named {column}. Columns: {names}. Choose one of them and check again.
err.column.description: An error shown in place of a result, the program's own words: the column asked for is not in the file; {names} is every column name of the file, joined by a comma and a space. It speaks as Knos, in the first person, and keeps the person's file; the Choose the column button follows it. Keep {column}, {names} as written; they are filled in.

btn.column.description: A next-step button under an error: goes to the column field.

act.why.text: Recorded because you pressed Yes, record it. Nothing was charged.
act.why.description: The line after a test payment: why it was recorded.

act.undo.description: The line after a test payment: the button that takes the payment back.

act.undone.text: The test payment is undone. Nothing was charged.
act.undone.description: The line after a test payment: after it is taken back.

act.undo_error.text: I could not undo the test payment, because some of its runs are already used. Nothing was charged.
act.undo_error.description: The line after a test payment: when it cannot be taken back.

offline.line.text: You are offline. This page was kept from your last visit.
offline.line.description: A line under the tool's name, shown only when the page was opened with no network and is the copy kept from the last visit.

res.input.description: The label of the table a result checked: in the box of a result page opened from its link, and over the read-only copy shown under the result after a run.

why.unknown_none.text: I could not compare any row with the limit, because no value in {column} is a number.
why.unknown_none.description: The reason line of a result Knos cannot tell when the program names no row: no value in the column is a number. Keep {column} as written; it is filled in.

why.unknown_one.description: The reason line under the result I cannot check: the one row whose cell in the column is missing or not a number. Keep {r}, {column} as written; they are filled in.

tool.sample_column.description: The made-up sample's column in plain words, shown in place of its file name capacity_ah on the rule line, in the evidence line and in the example in the box (the file name shows only in the fold How it works). Lower case: it is read inside a sentence.

fold.column.text: The sample's column {column} holds the battery's capacity in amp hours.
fold.column.description: A line inside the fold How it works: the sample's column as the file names it, and what it holds. Keep {column} as written; it is filled in with capacity_ah.
